parole.significato: to take possession (of something) without the owner's permission, seize, grab, steal, purloin, annex, usurp
parole.testo: Related to Karelian anastoa and Veps anastada. According to Aikio, the word represents a borrowing from Proto-Samic *ānēstētēk (compare Inari Sami änistiđ), itself from *(h)ānēs, itself borrowed from Proto-Finnic *ahnas (whence ahnas (“gluttonous, voracious”)).

parole.significato: to secure the load of a sleigh or ahkio
parole.testo: kaare- + -istaa; the root is probably a borrowing from Proto-Samic *kārëtēk.
Probably borrowed from Proto-Samic *mietē (for semantics, compare Northern Sami mieđis (“favorable”); for the final -o, compare visto).

parole.significato: face (front of the head of an animal)
parole.testo: Possibly borrowed from Proto-Samic *nāmē (whence Northern Sami námmi (“thin skin covering growing reindeer antlers”)). Cognate to Karelian noama (“face, mask”).

parole.significato: chord (part at the top or bottom of a roof truss)
parole.testo: paartaa + -e, from a dialectal paartaa (“to hem”), borrowed from Proto-Samic [Term?] (compare Northern Sami bárdit).

Probably sound-symbolic. The theory of a Germanic origin (such as a borrowing from Proto-Germanic *skrīkijaną) is unlikely. Alternatively, if the sense "to scream" is original, possibly a borrowing from Proto-Samic *reakōtēk (for the phonology, compare Lieksa), with later influence from riehua.

parole.significato: Stállu, an evil creature in the Sami mythology.
to seal, stuff (fill a seam/seams or gap/gaps)
parole.testo: tilk- + -itä, possibly from dialectal tilka (“scrap, patch (of cloth, etc.)”), which is probably related to tilkku. Aikio has proposed it to be a borrowing from Proto-Samic *tielkẽ, *tielkëtēk.
